paragraphs: A model of an environment should help predict what would happen under different actions. This paper argues that fitting historical transitions can fail even when predicting only one step ahead. The problem is selection bias: the behavior policy that collected the data influenced which actions and outcomes were observed. Consequently, accurate fitting of those observations can still mislead action selection.

The authors propose adversarial weighted empirical risk minimization, or AWRM. An adversarial policy searches for a data distribution under which the environment model predicts poorly. The model is then trained under that challenging distribution. This objective directs learning toward weaknesses that matter when policies consider alternative actions, beyond simply reproducing the historical transition data.

The practical implementation, GALILEO, is evaluated on two synthetic tasks, three continuous-control tasks, and a real-world application. The experiments report accurate counterfactual prediction and improvements in offline policy evaluation, policy improvement, and online decisions. These results support addressing data-collection bias as a distinct challenge from errors that accumulate over long prediction sequences.
neurips-2023-adversarial-counterfactual-.tldr: GALILEO trains environment models against adversarially chosen distributions to address selection bias and improve counterfactual prediction and decision-making.

paragraphs: An RNN is also a dynamical system: its internal state evolves as it processes a sequence. Changing its parameters can qualitatively change that evolution, an event called a bifurcation. This paper investigates whether such changes help explain sudden jumps in training loss, connecting optimization behavior to the structure of the network's dynamics.

For a particular class of ReLU-based RNNs, the authors prove that certain bifurcations are associated with loss gradients tending toward infinity or zero. They also introduce a heuristic algorithm for finding fixed points and repeating cycles, along with parameter regions where these behaviors exist and remain stable. The method returns exact solutions for the points and cycles it identifies, including cycles of high order.

The algorithm is used to examine RNN training, where generalized teacher forcing is found to avoid certain types of bifurcations completely. The contribution therefore combines a restricted mathematical explanation with an analysis tool. It helps connect abrupt training behavior to specific dynamical changes without claiming that every loss jump has the same cause.
neurips-2023-bifurcations-and-loss-jumps.tldr: The paper links certain RNN bifurcations to extreme gradients and introduces an algorithm for analyzing the dynamics behind training instability.

paragraphs: Text classifiers can learn associations that predict labels in their training data but fail after deployment. This paper studies prediction settings where a label is spuriously associated with an attribute. Its approach uses knowledge of the data's causal structure to create counterfactual training examples that simulate interventions on those misleading features.

The method combines example matching through auxiliary data with a difference-in-differences approach. A large language model represents a conditional probability distribution over text, supporting the construction of simulated interventions. The authors also discuss why counterfactual augmentation can have favorable sample requirements compared with importance reweighting, under the assumptions of the prediction problems they consider.

Experiments examine clinical diagnosis prediction from medical narratives, aiming for predictions that remain consistent across caregivers, alongside semi-synthetic data. The intervention-based augmentation improves out-of-distribution accuracy over the evaluated invariant-learning baselines. The findings support using causal structure to guide text augmentation when the relevant assumptions hold, rather than treating arbitrary textual variation as sufficient for robust prediction.
neurips-2023-data-augmentations-for-impr.tldr: Causally guided counterfactual text augmentation improves generalization in studied settings where labels are spuriously associated with an attribute.

paragraphs: Preference-based reinforcement learning lets an agent learn from judgments about which behavior is better when writing a reward function is difficult. A common approach first converts those judgments into a learned reward model, then optimizes a policy using that model. This paper targets the difficulty of recovering accurate rewards from preferences, especially judgments supplied by people.

The proposed algorithm learns a policy directly from preference data. It uses a contrastive-learning framework to construct a policy score, assigning higher scores to policies that agree with the supplied preferences. This removes the separate reward-modeling stage and makes preference agreement the basis for assessing candidate behavior.

On offline reinforcement-learning tasks with actual human preference labels, the algorithm matches or exceeds the evaluated preference-based methods. In the reported high-dimensional control tasks, it also outperforms offline methods supplied with ground-truth rewards. The authors additionally demonstrate language-model fine-tuning. Together, these findings show that the direct approach can work across control and language settings, without establishing that preferences always outperform explicit reward information.
neurips-2023-direct-preference-based-pol.tldr: A contrastive policy-scoring method learns directly from preferences and performs competitively in offline control and language-model fine-tuning.

paragraphs: When clients have different data distributions, the same shared learning objective may not serve every client equally well. Personalized Empirical Risk Minimization, or PERM, instead learns a distinct model for each client. It personalizes how local empirical losses are combined by estimating statistical differences among the clients' data distributions.

This makes the aggregation of training evidence specific to the distribution each model must serve. The authors connect this formulation to optimal statistical accuracy for the local distributions. To optimize all clients' objectives at scale, they introduce a distributed algorithm that shuffles models rather than relying on standard model averaging.

The approach also permits clients to use different model architectures, including networks with different parameter counts. That flexibility allows model choices to fit individual devices' memory and computational resources. The paper provides a convergence analysis and experiments supporting the paradigm's effectiveness. Its contribution joins statistical personalization with resource flexibility: both the evidence used for a client and the model assigned to it can differ across the distributed system.
neurips-2023-distributed-personalized-em.tldr: PERM personalizes distributed learning objectives and uses model shuffling to support clients with different data and computational resources.

paragraphs: A generated image can look convincing while failing to express parts of a complex prompt. This paper addresses both detecting those mismatches and using the detection results to improve generation. It starts from the observation that existing multimodal scoring models may overlook semantic errors as prompts become more complicated.

The proposed Decompositional-Alignment-Score separates a caption into distinct assertions. A visual question-answering model checks each assertion against the image, and the individual results are combined into an overall score. This gives both a measure of total alignment and more specific feedback about which requested content is poorly expressed.

In experiments, the score correlates more strongly with human ratings than traditional CLIP and BLIP scores. The authors also use assertion-level feedback in an iterative procedure that strengthens the expression of different prompt requirements in generated images. Human studies report an 8.7% improvement in overall alignment accuracy over the previous state of the art. The contribution connects more detailed evaluation with a practical route to refining image outputs.
neurips-2023-divide-evaluate-and-refine-.tldr: Checking individual prompt assertions with visual question answering improves alignment evaluation and supplies feedback for iterative image refinement.

paragraphs: Fast motion can blur a conventional camera image so severely that recovering motion cues from the frame becomes difficult. Spike cameras provide much finer temporal information, but their binary streams lack color and typically have low resolution and degraded image signals. This paper combines the complementary information available from these two sensor modalities.

The proposed model has branches for blurry RGB images and spike data, with information flowing between them. A content-aware motion attention module uses a learned mask to select relevant image information. A transposed cross-attention module then fuses features from the two inputs, allowing spike streams to guide reconstruction of a sharp color image.

The authors also create two synthetic datasets containing high-temporal-resolution spike streams, blurry frames, and corresponding sharp images for training and validation. Experiments show recovery of clear RGB images from highly blurred scenes and improvements over state-of-the-art deblurring methods in multiple tested settings. The approach matters because it combines temporal detail from spikes with the color and visual content of ordinary images.
neurips-2023-enhancing-motion-deblurring.tldr: A two-branch model combines spike-camera motion cues with blurry RGB images to improve deblurring in high-speed scenes.

paragraphs: This paper examines why transformer language models can succeed at impressive reasoning tasks yet fail on seemingly simple ones. It studies three kinds of compositional problems: multi-digit multiplication, logic grid puzzles, and a dynamic-programming problem. Each requires intermediate steps to be combined correctly, making them useful for investigating systematic problem-solving.

The authors represent tasks as computation graphs and break solutions into intermediate procedures. This gives them a structured way to measure complexity and inspect how models handle the pieces of a solution. Their empirical findings suggest that the tested models rely on matching linearized portions of these graphs, without necessarily acquiring a general procedure for solving the full problem.

The paper also develops theoretical arguments for abstract multi-step reasoning settings, showing how autoregressive performance can deteriorate rapidly as complexity grows. These arguments complement the experiments by explaining a possible source of fragile performance. The findings question whether success on familiar compositions demonstrates systematic reasoning, while preserving the distinction between observed model behavior and a universal limitation.
neurips-2023-faith-and-fate-limits-of-tr.tldr: Experiments suggest transformer reasoning can rely on matching familiar computation fragments, with performance potentially degrading sharply as compositional complexity increases.

paragraphs: Counting patterns inside a graph is a common privacy-sensitive analysis task. A difficulty is that these counts can have high global sensitivity, forcing methods based on that sensitivity to add substantial noise. More adaptive measures, including smooth sensitivity and higher-order local sensitivity, can improve accuracy but are often expensive to compute.

This paper shows that suitably good approximations to those sensitivity measures can still support private algorithms. The contribution concerns the computation needed to determine privacy-preserving noise, making more accurate approaches practical for a broader range of graph patterns. Previously, efficient polynomial-time methods were known only for a limited selection of subgraphs.

Using this idea, the authors develop faster private triangle-counting algorithms for real social networks that are also easy to parallelize. They provide a polynomial-time private algorithm for any constant-size subgraph using less noise than a global-sensitivity approach. For paths in special graph classes, they obtain further improvements. The result expands the available accuracy–computation tradeoffs while retaining the stated restrictions on pattern size and graph structure.
neurips-2023-faster-approximate-subgraph.tldr: Approximating sensitivity measures enables faster private subgraph counting with less noise than global-sensitivity methods.

paragraphs: For a fixed policy in a Markov decision process, this paper asks whether most possible trajectories can be captured within a small set of states. The authors call such a set a SafeZone. Its quality has two dimensions: how many states it includes and how likely a trajectory is to leave it.

These objectives need to be considered together. A useful zone should be compact while keeping escape probability low. Here, safety refers specifically to trajectories remaining inside the chosen set; the definition does not itself establish that the states represent harmless outcomes. The paper studies the computational difficulty of finding optimal zones and shows that the general problem is hard.

The authors therefore develop an approximation-learning algorithm with guarantees for both objectives. Its main result gives an approximation factor of almost two for zone size and escape probability, using polynomial sample complexity. This provides a theoretically controlled way to summarize where a policy's behavior is concentrated, while explicitly allowing some probability of leaving that region.
neurips-2023-finding-safe-zones-of-marko.tldr: The paper approximates compact state sets that contain most trajectories of a given policy, with guarantees on both size and escape probability.

paragraphs: This paper estimates a ground camera's three-degree-of-freedom pose relative to a satellite image of its surroundings. The challenge is linking visual content across very different viewpoints. The method learns dense, pixel-level correspondences, allowing supervision across the full image to capture geometric arrangements and visual appearances that connect the two views.

Separate convolutional networks extract ground and satellite features. Assuming a fixed camera height, the ground features are projected into a bird's-eye view for an initial geometric alignment. A residual convolutional block refines that projection, and RAFT-based flow decoders estimate correspondences between the refined features and the satellite features. A least-squares method then filters matching inliers and estimates camera pose.

Experiments report median localization-error reductions of 89%, 19%, 80%, and 35% on KITTI, Ford multi-AV, VIGOR, and Oxford RobotCar, respectively. These results support combining dense learned matching with geometric pose estimation. The fixed-height assumption is part of the alignment procedure underlying those reported gains.
neurips-2023-learning-dense-flow-field-f.tldr: Dense flow matching between projected ground features and satellite features substantially improves camera localization on four reported datasets.

paragraphs: Unsupervised face animation generates a video using the appearance of a source image and motion from a driving video. Existing motion models can capture broad facial movement but struggle with smaller changes around areas such as the lips and eyes. This paper addresses the resulting artifacts by learning coarse motion and finer refinements together.

The approach retains a local affine model for coarse facial movement and adds a module that learns the motion this model misses. It builds a structure correlation volume from keypoint features in the source and driving images. Those dense correlations provide the information used to estimate finer facial movement through repeated refinement from low to high resolution.

The refined motion is combined with the coarse estimate to generate each new image. Experiments on widely used benchmarks report the best results among the evaluated state-of-the-art baselines. The approach matters because it gives detailed local motion its own learned correction mechanism, while continuing to use the coarse model for the larger facial movements it already represents.
neurips-2023-learning-motion-refinement-.tldr: A learned motion-refinement module improves face animation by adding fine local movements to a coarse facial-motion model.

paragraphs: Visual data contain regularities in where objects appear and what shapes they take. Neural networks can learn these regularities implicitly, but spatial conditions that conflict with them may lead to inaccurate generated images. This paper seeks to model such visual priors explicitly and make sampling from them customizable.

The proposed VisorGPT converts spatial descriptions, including bounding boxes, human poses, and instance masks, into discrete sequences. It then learns their probability structure through likelihood maximization, borrowing the sequence-modeling approach used in language modeling. The authors also investigate prompts that bring these different spatial representations into a unified framework and guide the kinds of sequences generated.

Experiments demonstrate effective modeling of visual priors and extrapolation to novel scenes. The contribution is a way to learn and sample structured visual layouts using a generative sequence model. The authors suggest that discrete spatial representations could also help extend language-model learning toward the visual world; this broader integration is presented as a possibility motivated by the results.
neurips-2023-learning-visual-prior-via-g.tldr: VisorGPT learns visual layout priors from discrete sequences of boxes, poses, and masks, enabling prompt-guided sampling.

paragraphs: A dynamic video scene often contains large regions that do not move. Representing those regions independently across time wastes storage and computation. Masked Space-Time Hash encoding, or MSTH, uses this observation to reconstruct dynamic 3D scenes efficiently from either multiple viewpoints or a single-camera video.

The scene representation combines a three-dimensional spatial hash encoding with a four-dimensional space-time encoding. A learned mask controls their relative contributions at each location. An uncertainty-based objective guides that mask to reflect how important spatial and temporal information is there. Avoiding redundant operations in static regions reduces hash collisions and allows many space-time voxels to share compact hash tables more effectively.

The design also removes the need to fit many temporally redundant features independently, making optimization easier. The authors report convergence after twenty minutes for a 300-frame scene. Across their dynamic-scene evaluations, MSTH delivers consistently better results than previous state-of-the-art methods with twenty minutes of training and 130 MB of storage. These findings connect representation efficiency directly to reconstruction quality and training speed.
neurips-2023-masked-space-time-hash-enco.tldr: MSTH learns where temporal encoding is needed, reducing redundant storage and computation in dynamic 3D reconstruction.

paragraphs: Combining data across study sites can broaden the populations and rare events researchers can examine. It also creates difficulties: sites may have different patient characteristics, record different covariates, and need to preserve individual privacy. This paper develops a federated method for estimating causal treatment effects for a specified target population under these challenges.

The method adjusts for differences in covariate distributions and accommodates mismatched covariates across sites. Its auxiliary, or nuisance-function, estimation procedure is designed to be multiply robust and privacy-preserving. Transfer learning estimates ensemble weights that determine how information from source sites contributes to the target estimate. The authors establish efficiency and optimality properties for these weights under different scenarios.

Finite-sample comparisons show advantages in efficiency and robustness over existing state-of-the-art approaches. The authors also apply the method to CMS data to study how percutaneous coronary intervention affects hospital stay duration for patients with acute myocardial infarction. The application illustrates the estimation framework; the abstract does not state the direction or magnitude of that treatment effect.
neurips-2023-multiply-robust-federated-e.tldr: A federated causal-estimation method combines heterogeneous sites using privacy-preserving auxiliary estimation and learned source weights.

paragraphs: This paper investigates which computational models best resemble how primates anticipate the future of physical scenes. The authors compare several families of prediction networks against dense neural recordings and human behavioral measurements containing thousands of comparisons. Candidate models predict pixels, object-based representations, or internal representations learned by image and video foundation models.

Many advanced models perform poorly on these neural and behavioral tests, suggesting that increasing scale alone is insufficient. Neural responses are best predicted by models trained to forecast future states in the latent space of self-supervised foundation models trained on dynamic scenes. These models also approach neurons' ability to predict visually hidden environmental variables without explicit training for that capability.

The strongest overall agreement comes from prediction in representations learned for diverse first-person sensorimotor tasks. Those models reasonably match both human error patterns and neural dynamics across the tested scenarios. The findings suggest that mental simulation favors reusable visual representations shaped by interaction-relevant tasks, while remaining evidence about model–brain correspondence rather than a definitive identification of the brain's mechanism.
neurips-2023-neural-foundations-of-menta.tldr: Predicting future states in representations learned from dynamic sensorimotor scenes best matches the study's neural and behavioral evidence.

paragraphs: Gaussian process models use kernels to describe relationships between observations. Combining several kernels can appear to offer an interpretable breakdown of those relationships, but that interpretation depends on whether the components can actually be identified. This paper examines that question for additive Matérn mixtures in single-output models and multiplicative structures in multi-output models.

For the single-output case, the authors show that the least smooth Matérn component determines the mixture's smoothness. They also establish an effective equivalence between the mixture process and that least smooth component. None of the mixing weights or individual component parameters are identifiable, challenging interpretations that assign distinct meaning to the fitted mixture components.

For multi-output models, the paper studies a kernel formed by multiplying a shared scalar kernel by a covariance matrix. That matrix is identifiable up to an overall multiplicative constant, supporting this structure for modeling relationships among outputs. Simulations and real applications support the analysis. The findings make kernel structure a question of interpretability as well as predictive modeling.
neurips-2023-on-the-identifiability-and-.tldr: Additive Matérn mixtures have serious identifiability limits, while the studied multi-output covariance structure is identifiable up to scale.

paragraphs: Learning to solve partial differential equations involves mapping one function to another, rather than simply predicting a single number. Many neural approaches represent those functions on discretized grids or graphs. This can tie the learned computation to a particular sampling or geometry, creating difficulties when the shape of the domain changes.

CORAL addresses this issue with coordinate-based networks, also described as neural fields. Its design removes constraints on the input mesh so that the method can work with arbitrary spatial sampling and geometry. The aim is to make function-to-function learning less dependent on how the domain happens to have been discretized.

The authors apply CORAL to PDE solving, forecasting changes across space and time, and inverse problems such as geometric design. Evaluations show robust performance across resolutions and good results on both convex and non-convex domains, matching or surpassing state-of-the-art models. The contribution is a flexible representation strategy that supports several kinds of scientific prediction while accommodating varied domain shapes and spatial resolutions.
neurips-2023-operator-learning-with-neur.tldr: CORAL uses coordinate-based neural fields for PDE-related learning across varied spatial samplings, resolutions, and geometries.

paragraphs: Continual learning concerns learning as information arrives over time. This paper proposes treating that process itself as a sequence-modeling problem. The connection makes established sequence architectures available for continual learning and changes how the learning procedure is represented: an episode of continual learning becomes a sequence model's forward computation.

The sequence model is trained through meta-continual learning. At this outer level, it encounters multiple continual-learning episodes, learning how to carry out the process across sequences. This distinguishes training the sequence model from the continual-learning behavior that its forward pass performs within an episode. Transformers and efficient Transformer variants provide concrete implementations of the formulation.

Experiments cover seven benchmarks spanning classification and regression. The reported results suggest that sequence models are an attractive option for general meta-continual learning. The contribution is therefore both a conceptual reformulation and an empirical demonstration: methods developed to process sequences can be trained to implement continual learning, creating a direct connection between research on sequence architectures and research on learning over time.
neurips-2023-recasting-continual-learnin.tldr: Continual learning is formulated as a sequence model's forward pass, with Transformers trained across episodes showing promising benchmark results.

paragraphs: UNets are widely used inside diffusion models, and their long skip connections carry information between distant network blocks. Although these connections help information and gradients travel through the network, training can still be unstable. This paper investigates why reducing the coefficients on those connections can improve stability.

The theoretical analysis shows that skip-connection coefficients strongly affect forward activations, backward gradients, and robustness to input perturbations. Hidden features and gradients can oscillate over large ranges. Input sensitivity can also produce outputs far from their desired values, contributing to oscillating losses and gradients. The analysis identifies benefits from scaling the connections in each of these areas.

Motivated by these results, the authors introduce ScaleLong, a framework for scaling long skip-connection coefficients. Experiments on CIFAR10, CelebA, ImageNet, and COCO report more stable training and roughly 1.5-fold training acceleration across tested diffusion models with UNet or UViT backbones. The work connects a specific architectural adjustment to both a theoretical explanation and observed training improvements.
neurips-2023-scalelong-towards-more-stab.tldr: ScaleLong rescales long skip connections to stabilize diffusion-model training, with theoretical support and reported acceleration of about 1.5 times.

paragraphs: Histology images reveal tissue structure, while gene-expression measurements provide information about the molecular processes associated with that structure. Collecting expression profiles can be costly and time-consuming. BLEEP aims to predict spatially resolved expression from whole-slide H&E-stained tissue images by learning the relationship between these two forms of evidence.

The framework trains on a reference dataset containing paired image patches and expression profiles at micrometer resolution. Contrastive learning places both modalities in a shared, low-dimensional representation space. For a new image patch, expression is imputed using profiles from the reference dataset, connecting visible tissue appearance to previously measured molecular information.

The authors evaluate BLEEP on human liver tissue data collected with the 10x Visium platform and report significant improvements over existing prediction methods. These results support the potential for image-based expression prediction to make molecular analysis more accessible and less expensive. The reported evaluation establishes performance in that tissue dataset, while broader diagnostic and research applications are presented as opportunities enabled by the approach.
neurips-2023-spatially-resolved-gene-exp.tldr: BLEEP learns a shared representation of tissue images and gene-expression profiles to predict spatial expression from histology.

paragraphs: Compositional Explanations describe a neuron's behavior using logical formulas built from concepts. Their coverage is limited when alignment is checked only on the neuron's strongest activations. A formula that describes those responses may leave much of the neuron's behavior unexplained. This paper focuses on expanding the range of activations that explanations address.

The proposed Clustered Compositional Explanations combine the existing logical-explanation method with clustering and a new search heuristic. The goal is to approximate behavior across a broader activation spectrum. Extending explanations in this way creates additional problems associated with working across multiple activation ranges, which the authors explicitly formulate and address.

The paper also examines what insights the resulting explanations can provide and proposes desirable qualities for comparing explanations produced by different algorithms. Its contribution is a broader framework for analyzing neuron behavior, together with criteria for assessing the explanations. The intended improvement is greater coverage of activation behavior, while the explanations remain approximations rather than complete descriptions of what a neuron computes.
neurips-2023-towards-a-fuller-understand.tldr: Clustered Compositional Explanations extend concept-based neuron explanations beyond the strongest activations to cover a broader range of behavior.

paragraphs: This paper asks how producing intermediate reasoning steps changes what a Transformer can compute. It studies chain-of-thought through expressivity: whether a model architecture can represent solutions to particular problems. Circuit-complexity arguments establish barriers for bounded-depth Transformers that must directly output answers to basic arithmetic and equation tasks.

For those direct-answer settings, the authors show that model size must grow super-polynomially with input length. They then construct constant-size autoregressive Transformers that solve both tasks by generating intermediate derivations in a commonly used mathematical format. The distinction is that the model can carry out a sequence of reasoning steps as it generates text. The analysis also extends to a general class of dynamic-programming problems.

Experiments complement the constructions: in the tested settings, Transformers fail at direct answer prediction but consistently learn correct step-by-step solutions given sufficient demonstrations. The results connect intermediate generation to increased computational capability. They establish what the studied constructions can express and what the experiments learn, rather than guaranteeing that any prompted language model will reason correctly.
neurips-2023-towards-revealing-the-myste.tldr: Theoretical constructions show how generating intermediate steps lets constant-size autoregressive Transformers solve tasks that challenge bounded-depth direct-answer models.

paragraphs: Predicting program execution time can help compilers and autotuners choose effective optimization settings. Existing performance datasets often describe small program fragments, such as kernels or basic blocks. TpuGraphs instead targets full tensor programs running on TPUs, making the prediction problem closer to the scale of complete machine-learning computations.

Each example includes a computational graph, a compilation configuration, and the measured execution time under that configuration. A graph represents a workload's main computation, such as an inference step or training epoch. The programs come from open-source machine-learning workloads and include architectures such as ResNet, EfficientNet, Mask R-CNN, and Transformers.

The dataset contains 25 times as many graphs as the largest graph-property prediction dataset with comparable graph sizes. Its graphs are also 770 times larger on average than those in existing machine-learning program-performance datasets. This scale introduces challenges in training efficiency, scalability, and prediction quality. The contribution is a resource for learning performance models that must account for whole-program structure and compilation choices together.
neurips-2023-tpugraphs-a-performance-pre.tldr: TpuGraphs provides large tensor-program graphs, compilation configurations, and TPU runtimes for learning whole-program performance predictors.

paragraphs: Text-to-image diffusion models are commonly trained and evaluated at fixed image sizes, but users may request different resolutions and aspect ratios. This paper examines the defects that appear when models are used at other sizes. The authors observe incomplete objects at lower resolutions and repetitive, disorganized content at higher resolutions.

They establish a statistical relationship between the number of tokens and attention entropy, a property of how attention is distributed. This suggests that the amount of spatial information aggregated changes with image resolution. Their interpretation links low-resolution defects to insufficient spatial information and high-resolution repetition to redundant information.

Based on that account, the authors introduce a scaling factor intended to reduce changes in attention entropy across image sizes. The adjustment requires no additional training or fine-tuning. Experiments report better visual appearance, image quality, and text alignment. The contribution connects a measurable change in attention behavior to a practical adaptation method, while the proposed explanation for the observed image defects remains an interpretation of that relationship.
neurips-2023-training-free-diffusion-mod.tldr: An attention-scaling adjustment improves diffusion-generated images at varied sizes without additional training or fine-tuning.
